_comment: The baseline-protection deny list of DESIGN.md §10, as data. This is automat's OWN control set, not a third-party publication: there is no upstream document to hash, and the compiler records that absence explicitly rather than leaving an empty hash field that reads as verified provenance. Every control names the §10 bullet it implements in design_basis, and any action that §10 does not enumerate must say why it is here in extends_design — the compiler refuses to build otherwise, so an action cannot be quietly added to a protection control.

source.note: automat's own control set. The artifact's source hash is of THIS file, which is what the compiler read; there is no upstream publication, and the absence of an upstream hash is deliberate rather than missing.

baseline-automation.reason: automat's in-account automation role establishes and re-verifies the detective baseline; a control that blocks its own installation is not a control

controls.title: The configuration recorder keeps running
controls.statement: No principal in the account may stop, delete, or narrow the AWS Config configuration recorder automat deploys. The recorder is the account's own evidence collection; an account that can switch it off can stop being observed without leaving a trace of having done so.
controls.extends_design: config:PutConfigurationRecorder is not in §10's list and is denied anyway. Put replaces the recorder's recording group, so a principal that cannot Stop or Delete the recorder can still narrow it to record nothing — same outcome, no denied call. Denying Stop and Delete alone is a control an attacker steps around rather than defeats.

controls.title: The delivery channel stays intact
controls.statement: No principal in the account may delete or repoint the AWS Config delivery channel. A recorder whose delivery channel is gone or aimed somewhere the account controls is running and recording nothing an auditor will ever read.
controls.extends_design: config:PutDeliveryChannel is not in §10's list and is denied anyway, for the same reason as PutConfigurationRecorder: Put repoints the channel at a bucket the account itself controls, which ends delivery to the evidence bucket without deleting anything.

controls.title: The conformance pack stays deployed
controls.statement: No principal in the account may delete or modify the AWS Config conformance pack automat deploys from the control artifact. The pack is the detective half of the vended baseline; the account's compliance findings are only meaningful while the rule set that produces them is the one the artifact named.
controls.design_basis: DESIGN §10, bullet 1: conformance-pack delete/modify — config:DeleteConformancePack and config:PutConformancePack are those two operations' action names.

controls.title: The trail keeps logging
controls.statement: No principal in the account may stop, delete, or reconfigure a CloudTrail trail, or change which events it records. The trail is the record of what was done in the account, including what was done to the rest of this baseline.
controls.extends_design: cloudtrail:PutEventSelectors is not in §10's list and is denied anyway: event selectors decide which events reach the trail, so narrowing them silences the trail without stopping it. §10 also says the trail actions should be 'scoped to the baseline trail if one is deployed'; a shipped control set cannot name a trail ARN that does not exist until vend time, so the resource is * — which is stricter than the scoped form and therefore safe in the direction that matters, at the cost of also protecting trails the account created for itself.

controls.title: The account may not leave the organization
controls.statement: No principal in the account may remove the account from its organization. Every preventive control automat attaches is an organization policy, so an account that can leave takes its whole baseline with it — and does so in one call.
controls.extends_design: Deliberately carries NO exemption, not even for automat's own automation role. automat never calls LeaveOrganization — reclaim closes an account, it does not detach one — so an exemption here would be a hole with no use, and the one hole that would undo every other control in this set at once.

controls.title: The baseline roles may not be altered
controls.statement: No principal in the account may modify, delete, or re-permission the management-assumable role or automat's own automation role. Both roles are doors into the account that the organization, not the account, is meant to control; a principal that can rewrite either one's trust policy owns the account's relationship to its parent.
controls.design_basis: DESIGN §10, bullet 4: iam:Update*/Delete*/Put*/Attach*/Detach* on OrganizationAccountAccessRole and the automat automation role.
controls.extends_design: Two departures from §10's wording, both deliberate. (1) The partition is wildcarded (arn:aws*:) rather than fixed to arn:aws, so the control also holds in GovCloud — which for a CMMC-facing tool is not a hypothetical partition. (2) It carries NO exemption. Exempting the automation role would let that role rewrite its own permissions, which is a standing privilege-escalation path and the opposite of the least privilege the role exists to demonstrate; exempting the management-assumable role is not expressible at all, because an exemption may only name a literal role ARN with a real account id (see the exempt_principal_ref pattern) and a shipped catalog does not know the account id. The consequence is written down rather than engineered around: changing either role after vend requires detaching this policy from the OU first, which is a delegated-policy-admin action that lands in the evidence chain. See docs/open-questions.md Q13.

controls.title: The account root user is not a way to work
controls.statement: No action may be taken in the account by its root user. The root user cannot be given a permissions boundary, cannot be scoped by an IAM policy, and cannot be attributed to a person; every legitimate use of a vended research account is a role.
controls.design_basis: DESIGN §10, bullet 5: root-user usage deny, aws:PrincipalArn = arn:aws:iam::*:root.
controls.extends_design: The partition is wildcarded (arn:aws*:) rather than fixed to arn:aws, so the deny also matches a GovCloud root principal. Carries no exemption, and cannot acquire one: the exempt_principal_ref pattern admits only role ARNs, which is what stops an exemption entry anywhere in a merged control set from undoing this statement.
